headline: High: shared file/API workflows create leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt injection is lower because no direct bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot (agent_a) has no documented direct ingestion of Kotaemon (agent_b) outputs, and Kotaemon’s web UI/file workflows do not show a shared channel by default. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or operator-mediated transfer, so injection risk exists but is limited. Uncertainty remains because both are unverified docs-only profiles.
conditions: IF an operator copies Chatwoot messages into Kotaemon prompts without sanitization, prompt injection becomes feasible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared clipboard or shared workspace, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted support text into Kotaemon.
Use a sanitizing wrapper that strips instructions from pasted content.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces or VMs.
Train operators to treat customer messages as untrusted input.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys. Kotaemon also writes to ./ktem_app_data and uses broad network egress, so if Chatwoot content is imported into Kotaemon, sensitive data can persist or be transmitted. The shared-data pathway is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF Chatwoot conversations or exports are loaded into Kotaemon, customer data may be retained in ./ktem_app_data.
IF Kotaemon sends retrieved content to a remote model API, imported support data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep customer records out of Kotaemon unless redacted.
Use a local-only model backend in Kotaemon.
Restrict ./ktem_app_data to a separate encrypted volume.
Review outbound API destinations before enabling ingestion.
requires-engineering: implement field-level redaction before indexing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Kotaemon supports multiple instances plus file-backed state, while Chatwoot exposes integrations such as Slack, Shopify, and Linear. If they are pointed at the same mutable resources or shared API scopes, concurrent writes or conflicting updates can occur. The profiles do not prove a lock, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same ticketing or support backend, updates can race.
IF both agents are granted overlapping API credentials, one agent can overwrite the other's state.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent.
Limit each agent to read-only access where possible.
Use a single writer for shared records.
Add manual approval before writes to shared systems.
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking on shared objects.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can surface support content and integrations, while Kotaemon is a document/chat-transcript RAG system that may present retrieved text as answers. If Chatwoot output is fed into Kotaemon and then acted on without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into incorrect support actions. The pairwise handoff is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated summaries are used as authoritative input to Kotaemon, downstream answers can inherit mistakes.
IF Kotaemon outputs are copied back into Chatwoot replies without review, incorrect guidance can reach customers.
mitigations: Require human review before sending any generated reply.
Keep source citations visible in Kotaemon outputs.
Do not auto-import Chatwoot summaries into retrieval indexes.
Use a checklist for support-agent verification.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot processes customer data and interaction history, while Kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys with remote-model options. If regulated customer or EU personal data is moved from Chatwoot into Kotaemon, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR controls, so the safest supported judgment is medium.
conditions: IF EU personal data from Chatwoot is indexed in Kotaemon and sent to a non-EU model endpoint, residency risk increases.
IF support records are retained in Kotaemon longer than Chatwoot retention policy, deletion/export obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Avoid moving regulated data into Kotaemon.
Document retention periods for both systems.
Use region-appropriate model endpoints only.
Purge Kotaemon indexes on deletion requests.
requires-engineering: implement synchronized deletion/export workflows.
